title: Retention of Qualified Teachers in Schools
what_it_is: Retention of Qualified Teachers in Schools

sections.label: Teacher service and resignation rates
sections.summary: Teachers average 11 years in service, with resignation rates of about 2% to 3% yearly, and 3% to 4% in the first five years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: On average, our teachers have been in service for 11 years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The overall resignation rate for the entire teacher population has remained low at around 2% to 3% a year over the past decade.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Over the first five years of service, we see a slightly higher overall resignation rate of around 3% to 4% a year, on average.

sections.label: Teacher salary reviews 2012 and 2015
sections.summary: The last two salary reviews were in September 2012 and October 2015, with eligible teachers receiving monthly increases of 8% and 4% to 9%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The last two salary reviews were in September 2012 and October 2015, and eligible teachers had a monthly salary increase of 8% in 2012, and 4% to 9% in 2015, respectively.

sections.label: Teaching assistants and allied educators
sections.summary: A request asks if the Ministry would consider more teaching assistants, teacher aides or allied educators to help teachers with administrative duties, learning support and classroom management.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, I would like to ask if the Ministry would look into the employment and deployment of more teaching assistants, teacher aides or allied educators to assist our full-time classroom teachers to help them better manage the demands of teaching, particularly in terms of carrying out administrative duties, providing student learning support and even in classroom management.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Indeed, MOE is looking at increasing the number of allied educators for learning and behavioural support, and providing a variety of means to provide skills outside of just the teaching profession to allow the teachers to concentrate on the most important aspects of their profession.

sections.label: Teacher development and perceived value
sections.summary: Teachers' concerns include ongoing professional development of at least 100 hours yearly, and a survey showed many felt value and respect were decreasing but would continue teaching.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The concerns of teachers also include the opportunity to have regular ongoing professional development and that is something that we do have a significant amount of work going into ensuring that every teacher has at least 100 hours of professional development every year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Other concerns: one of the striking points in the survey was actually the perception of how they are valued and respected within society, and there was, interestingly, a big group of teachers within the survey who recorded that they felt that the value and respect that they were accorded were decreasing and yet this would not stop them from continuing with the teaching profession as they found this a very meaningful profession.
